intent: What an Avatar shows in place of its picture - initials or a glyph - while no image has loaded.
typical_uses: A person's initials, shown until their picture loads or when there is none
A colored identity circle for someone who has no picture

dont_use_when.situation: A placeholder while the record the avatar belongs to is itself still loading

invariants.text: The fallback renders whenever its Avatar's load status is anything but loaded - idle with no AvatarImage, loading, or error - and is removed from the DOM the moment the status becomes loaded.

With `delay`, the fallback stays out of the DOM for that many milliseconds after it mounts, so an image that loads within the delay never shows a fallback at all; once the delay has passed it follows the load status like a fallback without one. Without `delay` it can show from the first render.
`tone` and `variant` pick one of the twelve fill cells avatar.module.css shares with AvatarGroupCount, so a fallback and a count chip given the same pair paint the same colors.

anti_patterns.dont: Drive `tone` from a live state, such as danger for a suspended account or success for an online one
anti_patterns.do_instead: Derive `tone` from a stable identity (a hash of the user id, a team's assigned color) and show the state with AvatarBadge

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the fallback's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the fallback's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (imageLoadingStatus). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through avatar.module.css, not through this.

good.title: Initials behind a picture, held back briefly to avoid a flash
An identity fill for someone with no picture

bad.title: A tone switched by the person's status
bad.why: The circle changes color whenever the state changes, so the fill no longer identifies the person; keep `tone` tied to identity and put the state on an AvatarBadge.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, AvatarFallbackState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the fallback's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: AvatarFallbackState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the fallback's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (imageLoadingStatus). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through avatar.module.css, not through this.
